summary_paragraph: A man with a history of alcohol abuse, COPD, CAD s/p CABG, and esophageal stricture was admitted for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and hematemesis. He had recently undergone esophageal dilation and presented with signs of esophagitis and mediastinitis on CT imaging. Due to concern for microperforation, he was kept NPO and started on IV antibiotics (ceftriaxone and metronidazole) and TPN for nutritional support. An upper GI series ruled out frank perforation. His atrial flutter resolved with hydration, and he was managed without anticoagulation. Repeat CT showed marked improvement in esophageal inflammation, allowing a trial of sips, which he tolerated. He was discharged to extended care with plans to continue IV pantoprazole, antibiotics, and TPN, with follow-up in the GI clinic to reassess oral intake and medication restart.
